title: Kahana vs Discord: Keep the Chat, Add the Shelf
excerpt: Discord is real-time chat, voice, servers, and community velocity. Kahana is the shelf and reading list beside the chat, not another inbox.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: 250M monthly active users (MAUs) as of early 2026.
Annual revenue estimated around USD 561M–1.3B; valuation >USD 20B.
Used for gaming, creator communities, developer forums, and paid groups via Server Subscriptions.

strengths.title: Powerful real-time communication
strengths.detail: Voice channels, video calls, text channels, threads, and screen sharing, strong for synchronous interaction.

strengths.title: Scales to very large communities
strengths.detail: Supports communities up to 1M+ members per server, with roles, permissions, and moderation tools.

strengths.title: Free for most use cases
strengths.detail: Core features are free for owners and members; Nitro and server boosts add perks but aren’t required.

strengths.title: Rich feature set for communities
strengths.detail: Channels, roles, bots, webhooks, integrations, Stage channels, and events, strong for gaming, hobby, and creator communities.

weaknesses.title: Challenging UX for non-tech users
weaknesses.detail: UI can overwhelm; many channels, threads, and notifications make onboarding hard for mainstream or older audiences.

weaknesses.title: Not built for paid community businesses out of the box
weaknesses.detail: Server Subscriptions are limited and region-bound; payments, onboarding, and tiers often need external tools.

weaknesses.title: Weak search and long-term knowledge management
weaknesses.detail: Excellent for real-time chat; weaker as a knowledge base, finding and organizing information over time is painful.

weaknesses.title: Limited branding and customization
weaknesses.detail: Server name and icon only, no deep white-label, custom domains, or major changes to Discord’s look.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Discord is real-time chat, voice, servers, and community velocity. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Discord is the easiest way to talk over voice, video, and text.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Discord side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Discord you can use Memberships and Community & Messaging as first-class product jobs. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with Discord

You can use both. Discord keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on Discord. Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
